english.special_notes: English has 26 letters, 5 vowels (A, E, I, O, U) and sometimes Y, 21 consonants.

arabic.special_notes: Arabic is written right to left. 28 letters. Vowels indicated by diacritics. Letters change shape depending on position.

oromo.special_notes: Oromo uses Latin script called Qubee. No C, V, X, Z in native words but used in borrowed words. 5 vowel system.

somali.special_notes: Somali uses Latin script with 24 letters. C represents pharyngeal sound. No P, V in native words. 5 vowel system.

hadiyaa.special_notes: Hadiyya uses Ethiopic script (Ge'ez). Abugida system where each character represents consonant+vowel. 7 vowel orders per consonant.

wolayitta.special_notes: Wolayitta uses Ethiopic script. Also spelled Wolyitta. Abugida system where consonant shapes change with vowels. 7 vowel orders.

afar.special_notes: Afar language spoken in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Djibouti. Latin script. Known for guttural sounds.

gamo.special_notes: Gamo uses Ethiopic script. Abugida system where each character represents consonant+vowel. 7 vowel orders per consonant.

swahili.special_notes: Swahili uses Latin script. No Q and X in native words. C always pronounced as 'ch'. 5 vowel system.

kinyarwanda.special_notes: Kinyarwanda official language of Rwanda. Latin script. 5 vowels. No Q and X. Tone important.

kirundi.special_notes: Kirundi official language of Burundi. Very similar to Kinyarwanda. Latin script with 5 vowels.

luo.special_notes: Luo language spoken around Lake Victoria. Latin script. 5 vowel system. Tone distinctions important.

luganda.special_notes: Luganda uses Latin script. Double letters indicate gemination (long consonants). 5 vowel system with tone.

dinka.special_notes: Dinka uses Latin script with special characters (Ä, Ë, Ï, Ö, Ŋ, Ɣ). Vowel length and tone important.

nuer.special_notes: Nuer uses Latin script with special characters similar to Dinka. Vowel length and tone distinctions crucial.

korean.special_notes: Hangul has 14 basic consonants and 10 basic vowels. Letters combine into syllable blocks. Created by King Sejong in 1443.

hindi.special_notes: Devanagari script, written left to right. Consonants have inherent 'a' sound. Matras (vowel signs) modify consonants.

bengali.special_notes: Bengali script derived from Brahmi. Written left to right. Consonants have inherent vowel. Many conjunct characters.

telugu.special_notes: Telugu script is an abugida. Written left to right. Consonants have inherent 'a' sound. Many conjunct forms.

kurdish.special_notes: Kurdish uses Latin script (Kurmanji) or Arabic script (Sorani). Kurmanji uses Ç, Ş, Û, Ê, Î. 8 vowels.

farsi.special_notes: Persian uses modified Arabic script with 4 extra letters (پ, چ, ژ, گ). Written right to left. Short vowels usually not written.

german.special_notes: German has 26 basic letters plus Ä, Ö, Ü, ß. V sounds like F. W sounds like V. ß = sharp S.
